approaches_tried.approach: Live, non-dry-run /orchestrate --implement test directly against the real consumer repo's held task
approaches_tried.result: rejected in favor of a safer equivalent
approaches_tried.reason: The consumer repo has another active session's uncommitted work in flight (tasks 119/129). A live orchestrate dispatch would acquire a real task lock and write a real dispatch file there. Instead, proved the identical mechanism via two independent, non-mutating scratch fixtures: test-orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh's Group 33b (dry-run: a forced implement against a held candidate IS admitted and dispatched) plus a direct skill_preflight_update(task, "implement", session, "monotonic-max") call against a scratch state.json (the EXACT call orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh's live path makes), confirming status stays "hold" afterward. Together these cover the full real call chain without touching the shared consumer repo beyond the two writes the dispatch explicitly sanctions (the deploy itself, and generate-todo.sh's regeneration).

approaches_tried.approach: Redeploy this repo's (nvim's) own .claude/ tree to clear the 2 NEW test-status-vocabulary.sh/test-validate-state.sh harness failures
approaches_tried.reason: The dispatch's concurrency note explicitly prohibits a whole-tree redeploy mid-cycle while sibling task 292 has its own deploy phase still deferred ('phase 5 deploy deferred' per its own last commit). Both failures are confirmed non-regressions: Phase 1 already proved the underlying logic correct via direct source-store sourcing, and test-update-task-status.sh's source-store-first override technique proves the same class of staleness is purely a deploy-timing artifact, not a defect.
